source_refs.note: Topic 24.2 with its side box and Quick Check 24.2, as printed (PDF 120-122); the reaction schemes are redrawn. The book numbers the phenyl amine methods i, iii, iv.

blocks.text: i) Primary amines can be prepared by the nucleophilic substitution reactions of halogenoalkanes with ammonia. Excess of ethanolic ammonia under pressure is used to avoid the formation of secondary amines or a mixture of products.
If NH₃ is in excess, the major product will be primary amine and if halogenoalkane is in excess, tertiary amine is the major product.

blocks.alt: CH3-CH2-Br (bromoethane) + NH3 (excess), with ethanol over and High pressure under the arrow, gives CH3-CH2-NH2 (ethanamine) + HBr.
blocks.caption: Bromoethane and excess ammonia give ethanamine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 120).

blocks.text: ii) Primary amines are prepared by the reduction of alkanenitriles. For example, propanenitrile is reduced with H₂/Ni or LiAlH₄ ro prepare propane-1-amine

blocks.alt: CH3-CH2-C triple bond N (propanenitrile) + 4[H], with LiAlH4 over the arrow, gives CH3-CH2-CH2-NH2 (propan-1-amine).
blocks.caption: Reduction of propanenitrile to propan-1-amine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 120).

blocks.text: iii) Nitroalkanes are reduced in the presence of LiAlH₄ resulting in the formation of primary amines.

blocks.alt: CH3-CH2-NO2 (nitroethane) + 3H2, with LiAlH4 over the arrow, gives CH3-CH2-NH2 (ethanamine) + 2H2O.
blocks.caption: Reduction of nitroethane to ethanamine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 120).

blocks.text: iv) Alkanamides are reduced by LiAlH₄ to form primary amines in good yield since no byproduct is formed in this reaction.

blocks.alt: CH3-C(=O)-NH2 (ethanamide) + 4[H], with LiAlH4 over and H2O/H+ under the arrow, gives CH3-CH2-NH2 (ethanamine) + H2O.
blocks.caption: Reduction of ethanamide to ethanamine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 121).

blocks.text: v) Primary alkanamine can also be prepared by the Hofmann reaction.

blocks.alt: Hofmann reaction over two lines: CH3-C(=O)-NH2 + Br2 + 4NaOH gives CH3-NH2 + 2NaBr + Na2CO3 + 2H2O.
blocks.caption: Hofmann reaction of ethanamide (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 121).

blocks.text: This reaction yields the amine with one carbon less than the starting amide.
I) Secondary amines can be prepared by the alkylation of primary amines. When a halogenolkane reacts with a primary amine in the presence of ethanol under pressure secondary amine is formed.

blocks.alt: CH3-CH2-Br (bromoethane) + CH3-NH2, with ethanol over the arrow, gives CH3-CH2-NH-CH3 (N-methylethanamine) + HBr.
blocks.caption: Alkylation of methanamine with bromoethane (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 121).

blocks.text: ii) Secondary amines are also prepared by the reduction of N-substituted amides

blocks.alt: CH3-C(=O)-NH-CH3 (N-methylethanamide) + 2H2, with Ni/Pt over the arrow, gives CH3-CH2-NH-CH3 (N-methylethanamine) + H2O.
blocks.caption: Reduction of N-methylethanamide to N-methylethanamine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 121).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed reduction of N-methylethanamide shows ‘+ H₂’ and no water; it needs 2H₂ and gives water: CH₃CONHCH₃ + 2H₂ → CH₃CH₂NHCH₃ + H₂O, as drawn above.
i. Phenyl amine can be prepared by ammonolysis of chlorobenzene. Ammonylsis is a reaction in which an ammonia molecule is broken down to react with another compound.

blocks.alt: Chlorobenzene (benzene ring with Cl) + 2NH3, with Cu2O over and 250 degrees C, 50 atm under the arrow, gives phenylamine (ring with NH2) + NH4Cl.
blocks.caption: Ammonolysis of chlorobenzene to phenylamine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 121).

blocks.text: iii. Phenyl amine can also be prepared by the reduction of nitrobenzene.

blocks.alt: Nitrobenzene (ring with NO2) + 6[H], with Sn + Conc. HCl over the arrow, gives phenyl amine (aniline) (ring with NH2) + 2H2O.
blocks.caption: Reduction of nitrobenzene to phenyl amine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 122).

blocks.text: iv. Phenyl amine can be prepared by the Hofmann reaction.

blocks.alt: Hofmann reaction over two lines: benzamide (ring with C(=O)-NH2) + Br2 + 4NaOH gives phenylamine (ring with NH2) + 2NaBr + Na2CO3 + 2H2O.
blocks.caption: Hofmann reaction of benzamide (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 122).

blocks.title: Quick Check 24.2
blocks.text:
a) The “feel good factor” in chocolate has been identified as 2-phenylethanamine, C₆H₅CH₂CH₂NH₂. Suggest a synthesis of this compound from chloromethylbenzene, C₆H₅CH₂Cl.
b) What nitro compound, nitrile and amide are reduced to yield each of the following amine compound?
I) For the primary amine: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–Nh₂ (determine the structures of nitro compound, nitrile, and amide that would produce this amine upon reduction
ii) For the secondary amine: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–NH–Ch₃
